content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am trying to set up an integration but have not been successful so far. My goal is to establish TCP communication between a Banner XS26-2DE device and a [product_name] controller with [version_no], but I'm facing issues. I've contacted the Banner support team but they were unable to assist. I've also attached the manual for the Banner equipment. Thank you for any guidance.

The [product_name] controller is unable to work directly with the Banner device. It does not include libraries like those found in TIA Portal and does not support Profinet-I/O. The [product_name] controller is limited to Ethernet TCP/IP communication using the [version_no] protocol or, for versions [version_no] and above, Modbus TCP/IP.

So I would need a newer version of the [product_name] controller. Do you happen to have an example of how to map inputs and outputs for a device (not supplied by [company_name]) to communicate over Ethernet TCP/IP? Appreciate your assistance.
No, the remote device must support Ethernet TCP/IP using the [version_no] protocol. This is different from standard Ethernet TCP/IP communication.
Could you share an example for the [version_no] protocol? Thank you.
I'm afraid I can't provide that. The protocol is built into the firmware of the [product_name] controller.
So, does this mean the [product_name] controller cannot communicate with other devices, only those from [company_name]?

Not exactly. The remote device does need to support Ethernet TCP/IP using the [version_no] protocol. For instance, there are various apps or HMIs (from other manufacturers) that can handle this protocol.

One option is to use a [product_name] controller with [version_no]; these support Profinet connections and can communicate with a [product_name]. If you already have a [product_name] with extension modules, it's possible to add a small [product_name] CPU (without expansions) to act as a protocol converter, but you'll need additional configuration software. If safety functions of the Banner XS26-2DE are required, then a CPU with Profisafe capability is necessary; the [product_name] controller is suitable only for basic signaling and not for safety applications. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to integrate a third-party Banner device with a [product_name] controller using Ethernet TCP/IP. The main challenge is that the [product_name], particularly with [version_no], doesn't offer standard TCP/IP protocol support for devices outside its ecosystem, requiring specific communication protocols. This limitation causes confusion and restricts integration capabilities with third-party products.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] controller with [version_no] to support standard Ethernet TCP/IP communication for seamless integration with third-party devices. They are also looking for clear documentation and compatibility to facilitate successful exchanges of data.
